purpose: Tolterodine is used to treat an overactive bladder. It helps reduce the sudden urge to urinate, frequent trips to the bathroom, and accidental urine leakage. It can make a big difference in your daily comfort and quality of life.
how_it_works: Your bladder has muscles that can sometimes squeeze too often or too strongly, causing that urgent 'gotta go now' feeling. Tolterodine works by blocking certain signals in the bladder that cause those unwanted squeezes. Think of it like putting the brakes on an overactive bladder so it can hold more urine and you feel less urgency.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dry mouth, constipation, dry eyes, blurred vision, headache, dizziness, and an upset stomach. Dry mouth is the most frequently reported one — chewing sugar-free gum or sipping water can help with that.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, trouble emptying your bladder, kidney or liver problems, or stomach problems like slow digestion, as this medicine may not be safe for you. This medication can cause blurred vision and dizziness, so be careful when driving or using machinery. Older adults should use it with extra caution as it may cause confusion or memory issues. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated since this medicine can reduce sweating.
typical_dosing: The regular tablet (Detrol) is usually taken twice a day, while the long-acting capsule (Detrol LA) is taken once a day. A typical dose of the regular tablet is 2 mg twice daily, and the long-acting version is usually 4 mg once daily. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose depending on your health and other medications.
